data.narrative:
Lumaril is a seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Mark Elliot and Ben Duffield that has raised $12M to date. The valuation universe comprises one public comparable (277810.KQ) and eight private peers in the Robotics & Manufacturing sector, including Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, and Generalist AI.

Stage-progression methodology is applicable and yields a $30M implied valuation, applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier from the $12M raised proxy to model typical Seed-to-next-stage advancement. Peer-median triangulation is not applicable due to insufficient narrow-set comparables; while ten same-sector peers exist, filtering to same-stage, adjacent-stage, and similar-tier datapoints yields fewer than three observations, making sector-wide median comparison unreliable without risking material distortion.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $26M (low) to $34M (high), with a median of $30M. This range reflects sole reliance on stage-progression methodology. Key uncertainties include the absence of robust peer-based validation and dependence on the 2.5x multiplier assumption, which may not capture Lumaril-specific execution risk, technology differentiation, or market conditions. Additional method triangulation would require either closer same-stage comparables or disclosure of financial metrics enabling revenue or burn-rate based approaches.
